passages.text: And a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed in the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars on her head.
passages.sermon:
A great sign appeared in heaven.
A woman stood there.
She wore the sun as her clothing.
The moon lay under her feet.
She had a crown on her head.
The crown was made of twelve stars.
passages.original: Καὶ σημεῖον μέγα ὤφθη ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ γυνὴ περιβεβλημένη τὸν ἥλιον καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτῆς καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς στέφανος ἀστέρων δώδεκα

passages.text: She was pregnant and crying out in the pain and agony of giving birth.
passages.sermon:
A woman appeared in heaven.
She was clothed with the sun.
The moon was under her feet.
She wore a crown of twelve stars on her head.
She was pregnant.
She cried out in pain.
She suffered the agony of giving birth.
passages.original: καὶ ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα καὶ κράζει ὠδίνουσα καὶ βασανιζομένη τεκεῖν

passages.text: Then another sign appeared in heaven: a huge red dragon with seven heads, ten horns, and seven royal crowns on his heads.
passages.sermon:
A second sign appeared in heaven.
This sign was a huge red dragon.
The dragon had seven heads.
The dragon had ten horns.
Each of the dragon’s seven heads wore a royal crown.
passages.original: Καὶ ὤφθη ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ἰδοὺ δράκων πυρρός μέγας ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ καὶ κέρατα δέκα καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ἑπτὰ διαδήματα

passages.text: His tail swept a third of the stars from the sky, tossing them to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, ready to devour her child as soon as she gave birth.
passages.sermon:
A huge red dragon appeared in heaven.
The dragon had seven heads, ten horns, and seven royal crowns on his heads.
The dragon’s tail swept a third of the stars from the sky.
The dragon threw these stars to the earth.
The dragon stood in front of the woman.
The woman was about to give birth.
The dragon was ready to devour her child as soon as she gave birth.
passages.original: καὶ ἡ οὐρὰ αὐτοῦ σύρει τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀστέρων τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν γῆν καὶ ὁ δράκων ἕστηκεν ἐνώπιον τῆς γυναικὸς τῆς μελλούσης τεκεῖν ἵνα ὅταν τέκῃ τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς καταφάγῃ

passages.text: And she gave birth to a son, a male child, who will rule all the nations with an iron scepter. And her child was caught up to God and to His throne.
passages.sermon:
A woman gave birth to a son.
Her child was a boy.
This boy will rule all nations.
He will rule with an iron scepter.
God took her child up to Himself.
God brought the child to His throne.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔτεκεν υἱόν ἄρσεν ὃς μέλλει ποιμαίνειν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ καὶ ἡρπάσθη τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ πρὸς τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And the woman fled into the wilderness, where God had prepared a place for her to be nourished for 1,260 days.
passages.sermon:
The woman fled into the wilderness.
God had prepared a place for her there.
She stayed in that place.
People nourished her there for 1,260 days.
passages.original: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἔφυγεν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον ὅπου ἔχει ἐκεῖ τόπον ἡτοιμασμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἵνα ἐκεῖ τρέφωσιν αὐτὴν ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἑξήκοντα

passages.text: Then a war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.
passages.sermon:
A war began in heaven.
Michael is an archangel.
Michael led his angels.
Michael and his angels fought the dragon.
The dragon is also called the devil and Satan.
The dragon had angels with him.
The dragon and his angels fought back against Michael and his angels.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο πόλεμος ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὁ Μιχαὴλ καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ τοῦ πολεμῆσαι μετὰ τοῦ δράκοντος καὶ ὁ δράκων ἐπολέμησεν καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But the dragon was not strong enough, and no longer was any place found in heaven for him and his angels.
passages.sermon:
The dragon fought in heaven.
The dragon was not strong enough.
The dragon could not win.
No place remained for the dragon in heaven.
No place remained for the dragon’s angels in heaven.
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν οὐδὲ τόπος εὑρέθη αὐτῶν ἔτι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ

passages.text: And the great dragon was hurled down—that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was hurled to the earth, and his angels with him.
passages.sermon:
The great dragon was hurled down.
This dragon is the ancient serpent.
People call him the devil and Satan.
He deceives the whole world.
God hurled him to the earth.
His angels were hurled down with him.
passages.original: καὶ ἐβλήθη ὁ δράκων ὁ μέγας ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος ὁ καλούμενος Διάβολος καὶ Ὁ Σατανᾶς ὁ πλανῶν τὴν οἰκουμένην ὅλην ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἐβλήθησαν

passages.text: And I heard a loud voice in heaven saying: “Now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of His Christ. For the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down— he who accuses them day and night before our God.
passages.sermon:
A loud voice spoke in heaven.
I heard this voice.
The voice said that salvation has come.
The voice said that power has come.
The voice said that the kingdom of our God has come.
The voice said that the authority of His Christ has come.
The voice explained why these things have come.
The accuser of our brothers has been thrown down.
This accuser accused our brothers before our God.
He accused them day and night.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ λέγουσαν Ἄρτι ἐγένετο ἡ σωτηρία καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ Χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἐβλήθη ὁ κατήγωρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἡμῶν ὁ κατηγορῶν αὐτοὺς ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός

passages.text: They have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony. And they did not love their lives so as to shy away from death.
passages.sermon:
The people overcame the devil.
They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb.
They overcame him by the word of their testimony.
They did not love their lives more than God.
They were willing to die for their faith.
passages.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐνίκησαν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ αἷμα τοῦ Ἀρνίου καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς μαρτυρίας αὐτῶν καὶ οὐκ ἠγάπησαν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτῶν ἄχρι θανάτου

passages.text: Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you who dwell in them! But woe to the earth and the sea; with great fury the devil has come down to you, knowing he has only a short time.”
passages.sermon:
The heavens exist above the earth.
Many beings dwell in the heavens.
God rules in the heavens.
God has cast the devil out of heaven.
Therefore, heavens, rejoice.
All who live in the heavens, rejoice.
But the earth and the sea remain below.
Woe to the earth.
Woe to the sea.
The devil has come down to the earth and the sea.
The devil is very angry.
The devil knows he has only a short time left.
The devil acts with great fury.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο εὐφραίνεσθε οἱ οὐρανοὶ καὶ οἱ ἐν αὐτοῖς σκηνοῦντες οὐαὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν ὅτι κατέβη ὁ διάβολος πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔχων θυμὸν μέγαν εἰδὼς ὅτι ὀλίγον καιρὸν ἔχει

passages.text: And when the dragon saw that he had been thrown to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child.
passages.sermon:
The dragon is Satan.
Satan saw that he had been thrown down to the earth.
He began to pursue the woman.
This woman had given birth to the male child.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε εἶδεν ὁ δράκων ὅτι ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν ἐδίωξεν τὴν γυναῖκα ἥτις ἔτεκεν τὸν ἄρσενα

passages.text: But the woman was given two wings of a great eagle to fly from the presence of the serpent to her place in the wilderness, where she was nourished for a time, and times, and half a time.
passages.sermon:
The woman received two wings of a great eagle.
She used the wings to fly away from the serpent.
She flew into the wilderness.
She went to her own place in the wilderness.
There, people nourished her.
They cared for her for a time, times, and half a time.
She stayed away from the serpent’s presence.
passages.original: καὶ ἐδόθησαν τῇ γυναικὶ αἱ δύο πτέρυγες τοῦ ἀετοῦ τοῦ μεγάλου ἵνα πέτηται εἰς τὴν ἔρημον εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς ὅπου τρέφεται ἐκεῖ καιρὸν καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἥμισυ καιροῦ ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ ὄφεως

passages.text: Then from the mouth of the serpent spewed water like a river to overtake the woman and sweep her away in the torrent.
passages.sermon:
The serpent is an enemy of the woman.
The serpent opened his mouth.
The serpent spewed water from his mouth.
The water flowed like a river.
The water chased after the woman.
The serpent wanted the river to sweep the woman away.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ ὄφις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ὀπίσω τῆς γυναικὸς ὕδωρ ὡς ποταμόν ἵνα αὐτὴν ποταμοφόρητον ποιήσῃ

passages.text: But the earth helped the woman and opened its mouth to swallow up the river that had poured from the dragon’s mouth.
passages.sermon:
The earth helped the woman.
The earth opened its mouth.
The earth swallowed the river.
The dragon had poured the river from his mouth.
passages.original: καὶ ἐβοήθησεν ἡ γῆ τῇ γυναικί καὶ ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ στόμα αὐτῆς καὶ κατέπιεν τὸν ποταμὸν ὃν ἔβαλεν ὁ δράκων ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And the dragon was enraged at the woman, and went to make war with the rest of her children, who keep the commandments of God and hold to the testimony of Jesus. And the dragon stood on the shore of the sea.
passages.sermon:
The dragon became very angry with the woman.
The dragon left the woman.
The dragon went to make war against the rest of her children.
These children obey God’s commandments.
These children hold to the testimony of Jesus.
The dragon stood on the shore of the sea.
passages.original: καὶ ὠργίσθη ὁ δράκων ἐπὶ τῇ γυναικί καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν λοιπῶν τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτῆς τῶν τηρούντων τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ Καὶ ἐστάθη ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον τῆς θαλάσσης
